author: Harry
text:
Hi @Dante

The `error.status === 0 → result = true` branch isn't an accidental fail-open — it's our graceful-degradation path on purpose. It covers cases where the BE is unavailable for reasons **outside the user's control**:

* **Deployment windows on our side** — we use rolling updates, so brief random failures can hit a small set of in-flight requests during pod rotation; this branch is our buffer for those.
* Transient infra blips / connection drain.
* Unexpected upstream errors.

The sole intent of this branch is to protect user experience when our own service has a temporary issue — it isn't meant to relax auth in general**.** In all of these, we'd rather let a real Hana user reach the site than block them with what looks like an arbitrary auth error.
We've been running this in production and haven't seen any abuse — the exploit window is also narrow (Hana-only URL, attacker must force their own transport failure on a partner-issued link, payoff is only a single fabricated session).

**Given this, my proposal is to leave this code path as-is and not include it in the security fix.**
cc @Justin

author: Justin
text:
Followed up on PR #46 to make sure this decision survives the v2 port, not just the legacy code.

@Dante 's PR #46 records the rationale **in-code** in the legacy consumer (`auth-hana.service.ts`), which is exactly right for "don't change this in legacy again." But that comment does **not** travel to the v2 RR v7 port — and our source-of-truth migration plan (`docs/migration/v2-migration-plan.md`) still instructed the **opposite** (default fail-closed). A future Hana Phase H1 porter following the plan would have silently dropped this now-blessed graceful-degradation branch.

So I pushed one more commit onto the **same** PR #46 branch (`611bf57a`, docs-only, no behavior change) aligning the plan with this decision in three places:

* **§7 loader sketch** — wrapped `POST_HANA_VERIFY_TIME` in `try/catch` so a transport failure (no HTTP response) reproduces the legacy `status === 0` pass-through; a real HTTP error response still denies.
* **§7 security question #1** — flipped the recommended default from "fail-closed" to **RESOLVED keep-as-is**, citing Harry's rationale (17933) + my sign-off (17943), and noting the v2 loader must reproduce the pass-through.
* **§13** — OMH-631 marked resolved (keep-as-is, no behavior change), cross-referencing PR #46.

Net: legacy in-code comment + the source-of-truth plan now carry the same keep-as-is decision, so the v2 port can't quietly revert it to fail-closed.

Close criteria unchanged: once PR #46 merges (now carrying both the legacy comment and the plan alignment) and the description is updated (done), this can be closed. cc @Harry

text:
PR opened: https://github.com/ohmyhotelco/oh-admin/pull/242

Fix for the parent ELS-2040 photo reorder bug. Root cause: the upload new-slot inside `#dropList` was counted by Sortable.js when computing drag indexes (off-by-one), so reordering after upload injected an `undefined` item (blank tile) and saved the wrong order.

Verified on running app: upload A,B,C → drag C to front → Save persists [C, A, B], no blank tile, no `undefined` in payload. Applies to both `app-hotel-detail-photo` and `app-room-detail-photo`.

author: Harry
text:
@Lexi 

Sorry for reply late.

Consolidated response to your 6 points

## 1. View design ✅

Noted — We will define the table to support `V_PAYMENT_FUNNEL` and update the view yourselves later. No action needed from my side on this.

## 2. Drop `FRONTEND_ERROR_CODE` ✅

Final DDL keeps only `FRONTEND_ERROR_MESSAGE TEXT NULL`. FE error codes aren't stable enough for structured analytics; the message field carries the actual analytical value.

## 3. CCS classification + Pending duration ✅

### TIMEOUT detection

When a payment attempt has **no terminal event arriving**, for example:

* PG never sends a callback back to our backend (PG-side issue or network failure between PG and our server)
* User loses internet mid-payment
* User force-closes the browser, tab, or app entirely
* User abandons the PG page silently (no cancel signal observable)

we receive no `APPROVED`, `FAILED`, or `CANCELLED` signal at all. Without a fallback, the row would stay in `PG_CALLED` forever. We need a job to detect these "abandoned" cases so the attempt is closed out and removed from the "pending" funnel.

**How it works**:

* `@Scheduled` job runs every **5 min**
* For any attempt still in a non-terminal state (`INITIATED` / `PG_CALLED` / `AUTH_STARTED`) more than **30 min** after `PG_CALLED_DATETIME` → mark `STATUS_CODE='TIMEOUT'` + set `TIMEOUT_DATETIME = NOW()`
* The 30-min threshold is aligned with OnePay's session lifetime — after that, the PG can no longer complete the transaction anyway, so it is safe to declare TIMEOUT.

**Pending-duration precision**:

* `TIMEOUT` → `TIMEOUT_DATETIME` is set when the scheduler detects the row (somewhere between the 30-min threshold and 35 min). Pending duration is ±5 min — the imprecision is inherent because the user is gone and we cannot know the exact moment they gave up.

### Column changes vs the original spec

| Spec column | Proposed change | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pg_called_at`  | Keep (rename to `PG_CALLED_DATETIME`, oh-api convention)  | "Pending starts" anchor  |
| `auth_started_at`  | **DROP**  | same `pg_called_at`  |

### Other naming-only changes (no semantic change)

* `attempt_id` → `ATTEMPT_SEQ` (PK suffix)
* `status` → `STATUS_CODE` (avoid SQL reserved word)
* `created_at` → `FIRST_INSERT_DATETIME` + add `FIRST_INSERT_UNO`
* `updated_at` → `LAST_UPDATE_DATETIME` + add `LAST_UPDATE_UNO`
* All other columns: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; `DATETIME(3)` → `DATETIME` (oh-api uses second precision)

These rename changes don't affect logic — same fields, just renamed to fit existing system conventions. No data is lost.

## 4. CANCEL_TYPE — verified by source review

After tracing our ohmyhotel pc, mobile proposed enum (only values we can actually capture):

| Value | Source | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POPUP_CLOSE`  | PC NicePay SDK popup close | ✅ Already wired in PC |
| `BACK_NAVIGATION`  | Mobile: user pressed back on PG page → returns to /payment (Android hardware back, iOS swipe, mobile browser back). FE checks for unresolved attempt on page reload and marks cancelled.  | ✅ FE-only work, no native bridge needed  |

`TAB_CLOSE` NOT feasible on mobile redirect — and not needed. Once the user is on the PG's page (full-page redirect, not a popup), ohmyhotel-mobile is unloaded from the tab — closing the tab can't fire any listener because our code isn't there. Physical limitation, not a coding gap.

**Recommendation**: for mobile, use `BACK_NAVIGATION` only. When the user presses back from the PG page, the tab returns to /payment, our FE runs again, detects the unresolved attempt, and marks it cancelled. This captures the typical "user gave up" intent on mobile without TAB_CLOSE. Are you OK dropping `TAB_CLOSE` from the mobile enum entirely?

## 5. Error vs Timeout distinguishable ✅

Schema separates `STATUS_CODE` from `CCS_CODE`:

* All timeouts: `WHERE STATUS_CODE = 'TIMEOUT'`
* Pure system errors: `WHERE STATUS_CODE = 'FAILED' AND CCS_CODE = 'CCS99'`

## 6. NicePay code lists  ✅

---

Could you confirm the points above? If there are no further concerns, when would you like us to start the implementation? Thank you!

@Calvin
Currently, encryption in transit is enabled for our ElastiCache, but TLS is not set as “required.”

The reason we did not make TLS required for access-control this time is that changing it from the current default would also require code changes, and it could affect both existing production clusters, cache-omh-cluster-v1 and cache-omh-cluster-v2.

So we are keeping it off for now, but we should update all of them later.
